issues.legal_issue: A tenant seeking to defeat eviction for erecting a permanent structure must specifically plead and establish the landlord’s written consent.
material_facts: The tenant erected a permanent structure on the rented premises.
The landlord pleaded that the structure had been erected without written consent.
The tenant’s written statement asserted generally that the landlord had consented, but did not specifically plead that written consent had been given or provide its particulars.
The tenant did not produce the alleged written consent.
issues.conclusion: The tenant failed to establish the required written consent, and the eviction ground was sustained.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(1)(b) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947 entitles a landlord to recover possession where a tenant has erected a permanent structure without the landlord’s written consent. When the landlord positively pleads the absence of written consent, the tenant must specifically plead the alleged consent and its particulars; a vague denial does not suffice. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: eviction_proceeding and permanent_structure_erected and landlord_pleaded_no_written_consent and tenant_failed_specific_consent_pleading and tenant_failed_to_establish_written_consent

predicates.eviction_proceeding: The matter is an eviction proceeding concerning a tenant’s occupation of rented premises.
predicates.permanent_structure_erected: The tenant erected a permanent structure on the rented premises.
predicates.landlord_pleaded_no_written_consent: The landlord alleged that the tenant erected the structure without the landlord’s written consent.
predicates.tenant_failed_specific_consent_pleading: The tenant did not specifically plead that the landlord gave written consent or set out particulars of that consent.
predicates.tenant_failed_to_establish_written_conse: The tenant did not produce or otherwise establish the alleged written consent.
predicates.eviction_ground_sustained: The ground for eviction based on the tenant’s construction was upheld.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding concerns a tenant’s permanent construction, the landlord pleads absence of written consent, and the tenant neither specifically pleads nor establishes that consent, the eviction ground is sustained.

issues.legal_issue: A request to obtain evidence from a public authority may be refused when it is first pursued belatedly during a supervisory proceeding after the party failed to seek the evidence in the trial court.
material_facts: The tenant claimed that the landlord’s written consent was held in municipal records.
The tenant did not seek an order from the trial court to summon those records, although copies had reportedly been unavailable.
The tenant also made no effort to produce the alleged consent during the appeal.
The tenant sought to summon the records only during the hearing of a petition under Article 227 of the Constitution.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was justified in refusing the belated request to summon the records, and there was no basis to interfere with that refusal.
issues.legal_principle: A party who could have sought relevant records from their custodian in the trial court should not obtain indulgence for a belated request made during a proceeding under Article 227, particularly when no effort was made to produce the material before the appellate court. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: supervisory_proceeding and party_claimed_relevant_public_records_exist and party_failed_to_seek_records_at_trial and party_failed_to_produce_records_on_appeal and party_requested_records_only_during_supervisory_hearing

predicates.supervisory_proceeding: The party seeks relief in a proceeding supervising a lower court’s decision.
predicates.party_claimed_relevant_public_records_ex: The party asserted that relevant evidence was held in records maintained by a public authority.
predicates.party_failed_to_seek_records_at_trial: The party did not ask the trial court to obtain the records from their custodian.
predicates.party_failed_to_produce_records_on_appea: The party made no effort to produce the records during the appeal.
predicates.party_requested_records_only_during_supe: The party first sought to summon the records during the hearing of the supervisory proceeding.
predicates.belated_record_request_properly_refused: The court’s refusal to permit the late request to obtain the records was upheld.

issues.definition: When a party in a supervisory proceeding claims relevant public records exist but did not seek them at trial or produce them on appeal, a request made only during the supervisory hearing is properly refused.
